purpose: Descriptive blinded code-quality review; no scored criteria or primary results changed

parser_pair.assessment: Both are direct causal fixes with equivalent regex expressions; only comments and formatting differ.
parser_pair.mechanism: The added negative delimiter lookahead is applied to each whitespace character in the option-name separator. It prevents configured space/tab delimiters from being swallowed by the greedy whitespace run. The change is applied to both ordinary and optional-no-value templates.
parser_pair.preserved_surface: Non-delimiter whitespace remains usable inside an option name; surrounding value parsing, strict behavior and interpolation code are not changed in these hunks.
parser_pair.quality: Fits the existing regex-template style. No new helper, abstraction, fixture-dependent constant or unrelated production edit appears.
parser_pair.comparison: Functional tie. parser-Y uses a slightly shorter explanatory comment; this is a minor readability difference, not a correctness or promotion finding.

csv_pair.assessment: Identical direct constructor fixes for DictReader and DictWriter.
csv_pair.mechanism: iter(fieldnames) is fieldnames identifies ordinary one-shot iterators and list(fieldnames) consumes them into a reusable schema. Reusable lists do not satisfy that identity check, so their original object/reference is preserved for external updates. The None guard leaves DictReader header discovery unchanged.
csv_pair.preserved_surface: The shown changes leave restkey/restval, extrasaction, dialect and quoting logic untouched; materializing the schema supplies the repeated iteration/length operations these implementations need.
csv_pair.quality: Two small matching constructor guards fit the current code. No fixture-specific values, unrelated production changes or extra abstraction appear.
csv_pair.comparison: Exact tie: both projected patches have the same SHA256.
